stem:
Meena pours all the water from a tall, narrow bottle into a short, wide jug. The jug is only half full, while the bottle was completely full.

What should Meena conclude about the volume of the water?

options.text: The volume of water decreased because the jug is only half full.
The volume of water stayed the same because the same water now occupies a different-shaped space.
The volume of water increased because the jug is wider than the bottle.
The volume of water became equal to the full capacity of the jug.

teacher.key_rationale: Volume is the space occupied by the water, not the container's capacity or fill level. The same water poured into a different container keeps the same volume, so B is correct. A confuses fill level with amount, C confuses container width with volume, D confuses capacity with occupied space.
